newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 23.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on December 23. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Suharto has said priority should be given to lessening the number deaths among women who give birth.

Indonesian business leaders have called for the transparent administration of a compulsory two percent levy on taxable income that must be donated by wealthy individuals and corporations under a recent presidential decree.
State Minister of National Development Planning Ginandjar Kartasasmita said on Saturday the country's economy would improve slightly next year after losing ground this year.
President Suharto said on Sunday big businesses which failed to give two percent of their after-tax incomes to the poor would be "morally chastised."

The Lippo Group plans to take a majority position in PT Matahari Putra Prima through its subsidiary PT Multipolar after making a tender offer for a 5.1 percent stake in one of Indonesia's largest department store retailers.

Transport authorities hope the backlog of trucks trying to cross the Sunda Strait to Sumatra, but stuck at the Merak port in West Java after recent inclement weather, should be cleared within two days after a special roll-on roll-off ship was chartered.
